newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal recognises new Congo, urges elections.
newsitem.headline: Portugal recognises new Congo, urges elections.

text.p: Portugal on Monday recognised the new Democratic Republic of Congo proclaimed after the victory of Laurent Kabila's rebels and appealed for democratic elections as soon as possible.

"Portugal reiterates its willingness to establish (with the new government) a relationship based on historical ties of friendship and cooperation that unite the two states, based on the principles of international law," said a foreign ministry statement.
The Portuguese government congratulated the way in which the Zaire rebels had "permitted a transition without generalised violence".

"The Portuguese government reiterates its willingness to cooperate with the authorities of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the international community in a democratic transition in which all representative parties take part, with a view to holding free and fair elections as soon as possible," it said.

"The Portuguese government appeals to the authorities of the Democratic Republic of Congo to take all measures to ensure respect for human rights and to assist in providing free access of humanitarian aid to refugees."
Following a seven-month civil war in Zaire, Kabila on Saturday changed the name of the country to the Democratic Republic of Congo and declared himself its leader.
He acted as his rebels entered Kinshasa, a day after Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko relinquished power and abandoned his capital.
